asks: Calgary and District Labour Council asks the commission to wait for the 2026 census or use 2024 population estimates, keep Calgary and Edmonton districts inside city limits, and allot seats by place: Calgary 28, Edmonton 21, Red Deer 2, Lethbridge 2, a seat plus a hybrid seat each for Medicine Hat, Airdrie and St. Albert.

quote: Airdrie should have a seat and a hybrid seat.
note: One Airdrie-only seat plus one urban-rural hybrid seat; no boundaries given. Also says Calgary shares no interests with surrounding cities and should have no urban-rural hybrids (pp. 103-104), which cuts against a Calgary-Airdrie district, but Airdrie is not named in that passage so no rejects coded.
Cochrane only named in the list of communities the council represents. General statement that Calgary's boundaries should be used and Calgary should have no hybrids names no place.
Chestermere ('Chestemere') only named in the list of communities the council represents.

quote: Red Deer should have two seats. Lethbridge should have two seats.
note: Seat table (p. 102) marks hybrid seats with an asterisk; Red Deer's two seats carry none, so two city seats. No boundaries described.

quote: Red Deer should have two seats. Lethbridge should have two seats.
note: Seat table (p. 102) marks hybrid seats with an asterisk; Lethbridge's two seats carry none, so two city seats. No boundaries described.

quote: St. Albert should have a seat and a hybrid seat.
note: One city seat and one hybrid seat, nothing more said.

asks: City of Airdrie asks for two Airdrie-centred districts (north-south or east-west), possibly with Crossfield and nearby rural polls, and supports a separate Cochrane district that could include Bearspaw.

quote: In addition to the city boundaries of Airdrie and the Town of Crossfield, our proposed scenarios could incorporate some rural voting stations in the areas surrounding Airdrie.
note: Three scenarios, all two Airdrie-centred districts with some surrounding rural area; Scenario 3 (east-west, Crossfield in Airdrie East) is closest to the particulars of A1. Scenario 1 is a north-south split. Also says 'we recommend dedicated Airdrie constituencies' (p. 168). Maps on pp. 170-179 not legible in OCR; text carries the request. Submission text appears twice (pp. 163-169 and 180-186).

quote: We would support the creation of a dedicated Cochrane electoral division that could include the Bearspaw area, which has strong community ties to Cochrane.
would allow Crossfield to be included in a primarily urban riding instead of the primarily rural riding of Olds-Didsbury-Three Hills where it currently sits
note: Partial request: Crossfield moved from Olds-Didsbury-Three Hills to an Airdrie district (in two of three scenarios); suggests Bowden could then move into Olds-Didsbury-Three Hills. Nothing on Sundre or Mountain View County.

asks: MLA for Lethbridge-East asks the commission to explore combining the two Lethbridge districts with parts of the adjacent rural divisions into three or four urban-rural ridings.

quote: Lethbridge-West, and logical portions of the adjacent rural divisions listed above into three or four ridings focused on shared agricultural and economic interests
note: Asks for 'three or four' hybrid ridings drawing together Lethbridge-East, Lethbridge-West and parts of Livingstone-Macleod, Cardston-Siksika and Taber-Warner; no lines given, so direction.

asks: Medicine Hat resident asks that Medicine Hat be its own single urban riding, not divided between two urban-rural ridings.

Lethbridge resident (Deputy CAO of Coaldale) asks that Cardston-Siksika, Livingstone-Macleod, Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West be replaced by four city-and-country divisions: Lethbridge-Cardston, Lethbridge-Livingstone, Lethbridge-Little Bow and Lethbridge-Taber.

quote: the current divisions of Cardston-Siksika, Livingstone-Macleod, Lethbridge-East, and Lethbridge-West with four new divisions
note: Four named hybrid ridings each taking a part of the city (Annex B, p. 193, gives the city population in each). Same proposal as EBC-2025-1-0146.

asks: MLA for Edmonton-North West describes the constituency's boundaries and community cohesion; no explicit request beyond noting its fast growth.
Leduc County resident asks that the City of Leduc, Beaumont and Leduc County remain together in one electoral district.
Mayor of Spruce Grove asks for an electoral division aligned with Spruce Grove's city boundaries, separated from Stony Plain and extended east to Edmonton's limits.

Lethbridge County resident (CAO of Coaldale, writing privately) asks that Cardston-Siksika, Livingstone-Macleod, Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West be replaced by four divisions: Lethbridge-Cardston, Lethbridge-Livingstone, Lethbridge-Little Bow and Lethbridge-Taber.

quote: Siksika, Livingstone-Macleod, Lethbridge-East, and Lethbridge-West with four new electoral divisions, for which I have more clearly referenced in the attached diagrams
note: Same four-riding proposal and annexes as EBC-2025-1-0142 (campaign in substance; wording differs).

asks: Sherwood Park resident asks that Cambrian Crossing and Bremner be included in the Strathcona-Sherwood Park riding.
Former MLA for Medicine Hat asks for two south-east constituencies without Brooks: Medicine Hat North (city north of Highway 1) and Medicine Hat-Cypress-Forty Mile.
Calgary resident asks that Calgary-Foothills stay as it is, inside Calgary's city limits, and that the two new ridings go to north Calgary and south Edmonton.
Medicine Hat resident asks that Medicine Hat become one urban constituency with one MLA, not grouped with Brooks or rural areas.
Lethbridge resident asks that Lethbridge be divided into three ridings.

quote: Lethbridge needs to be divided into three ridings to better serve 100,000 people.
note: Three ridings for Lethbridge; does not say whether inside the city or joined to country, so neither L1 nor L3 fits.

note: One Airdrie-only seat plus one urban-rural hybrid seat; no boundaries given. Near-copy of EBC-2025-1-0138 (campaign: labour council template).

asks: Edmonton resident asks that every riding's population be kept within 10% of the average where possible.
President of the St. Albert NDP constituency association asks that the St. Albert and Morinville-St. Albert ridings stay as they are and that new seats go to south Edmonton and north Calgary.

quote: In my opinion, St. Albert and Morinville- St. Albert ridings should remain status quo.
note: Also warns against ridings 'split too significantly between urban and rural' and says there is 'strong support to leave the current ridings as is'.
Named only as a comparison (cities with two ridings).

asks: Alberta Federation of Labour asks the commission to use current population estimates, add two seats each to Calgary and Edmonton, keep two seats each in Red Deer and Lethbridge, give Medicine Hat one city seat, and keep Central Peace-Notley and Lesser Slave Lake as special districts with redrawn boundaries.

quote: Maintain the 2 seats in Red Deer • Maintain the 2 seats in Lethbridge
note: Maintain the existing two seats.

quote: Maintain the 2 seats in Red Deer • Maintain the 2 seats in Lethbridge
note: Maintain the existing two seats.

quote: Airdrie 1 Seat and 1 Hybrid Seat St. Abert 1 Seat and 1 Hybrid Seat
note: From the seat table: one Airdrie seat and one hybrid seat; no boundaries given. Text also notes one Airdrie district is over the 25% limit (p. 24).

quote: Airdrie 1 Seat and 1 Hybrid Seat St. Abert 1 Seat and 1 Hybrid Seat
note: From the seat table ('St. Abert' sic): one seat and one hybrid seat.

quote: we concede that those electoral districts will remain as the two districts covered by section 15(2) of the Act
note: Accepts Lesser Slave Lake remaining a section 15(2) district, but says its boundaries must be redrawn because it is now more than 50% below average (pp. 22, 25). A concession more than a request.

asks: Ardrossan resident asks that the Strathcona-Sherwood Park and Fort Saskatchewan-Vegreville boundaries be adjusted so growing 'rurban' Ardrossan and Fort Saskatchewan are separated from the rural east.
Sturgeon County resident asks that Morinville-St. Albert remain unchanged.

quote: boundaries were changed in 2019 for the better and should remain unchanged my opinion
note: Values the urban-rural mix of the Morinville-St. Albert hybrid.

asks: MLA for Calgary-Varsity asks that municipal boundaries be maintained and like communities kept whole and together within Calgary-Varsity.
Edmonton councillor asks that provincial boundaries align with municipal boundaries and that southeast Edmonton receive a new seat.
MLA for Calgary-Glenmore asks that Calgary-Glenmore's communities (including ties with Tsuut'ina) be kept together and municipalities kept whole.
Medicine Hat resident asks that Brooks-Medicine Hat revert to a mainly urban Medicine Hat riding, with the rest of the city in Cypress-Medicine Hat.
Town of Crossfield asks the commission to adopt one of the City of Airdrie's scenarios, particularly those placing Crossfield in an Airdrie-focused division.

quote: The Town of Crossfield strongly encourages the Commission to consider and adopt one of the City of Airdrie’s proposed scenarios as part of this important redistribution process.
note: Endorses the City of Airdrie's scenarios (EBC-2025-1-0139): two Airdrie-centred districts, with Crossfield in one. Does not restate the lines.

quote: Crossfield supports the City of Airdrie’s proposed redistribution scenarios, particularly those that include the Town of Crossfield within new Airdrie-focused electoral divisions.
note: Partial request: Crossfield with Airdrie rather than its current Olds-Didsbury-Three Hills riding (not named in the letter).

asks: MLA for Calgary-Edgemont asks that Dalhousie, Edgemont, Hamptons and Ranchlands be kept together and notes the split of Citadel causes confusion.
Writer suggests Church Ranches, Bearspaw and Watermark in Rocky View County as a natural fit to add to Calgary-North West.

note: Cochrane named only as the end of a bike path; the request is to join Bearspaw-area communities to Calgary-North West, with nothing asked about Cochrane.

asks: Edmonton councillor asks the commission to start from Edmonton's city limits, divide the city into ridings inside them, and give Edmonton one of the two new seats.

note: St. Albert named only as a place whose residents he imagines feel the same about being represented by their own; no request.

asks: President of the Alberta NDP asks that like communities be kept together, municipal boundaries respected, and new seats added in north Calgary and south Edmonton.

note: Only 'a Lethbridgian' as an example of municipal identity; no request about Lethbridge.
